practices_evaluation.justification: The test performs a single action (construction of Grafo) and contains a single Arrange-Act (creation) step with no multiple distinct Act operations; it focuses on one behavior.

The test uses only local variables and does not rely on shared mutable state; no setup/teardown annotations are required for this single short test and no static instance variables are referenced in the method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: There is only a single happy-path test creating a Grafo instance; no test for error/exceptional cases or assertions expecting exceptions are present.
The test only constructs an object with no input parameters or numeric ranges to validate; there are no obvious boundary values to test for the constructor case shown.
The test is short (<10 lines) and does not duplicate code; no helper methods are needed for this trivial constructor test and no duplicated blocks are present within the class snippet.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method is small (few lines), contains no loops or conditionals, and follows a simple linear flow (Arrange-Act); cyclomatic complexity is minimal.
The test contains no assertions (or only superficial checks); it lacks comprehensive assertions verifying multiple properties of the created object, reducing its ability to detect faults.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods are present; the test is active and runnable.
Method-level Javadoc explicitly references 'REQ-001', providing direct traceability between the test and a requirement.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test includes an explicit timeout (@Test(timeout = 4000)), which is an explicit performance-related test configuration and therefore qualifies as evidence of performance consideration per evaluation rules.

The method name is generic ('test0') and does not follow descriptive naming conventions (method_scenario_expectedResult) despite the Javadoc; name fails to communicate the scenario and expected outcome.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The class imports EvoSuite-specific artifacts, uses EvoRunner and EvoRunnerParameters, and the method is named 'test0' — these are signs of heavy test-code generation rather than minimal, intention-revealing tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The method Javadoc uses Given-When-Then phrasing indicating BDD-style design intent (Given/When/Then), which is evidence of thoughtful test design and prioritization.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test exercises a public API (public constructor) and does not probe internal implementation details or use reflection; it verifies observable behavior and is not tightly coupled to internals.
There are no assertions in the test method; assertions lack descriptive messages and specific checks which reduces diagnostic value when failures occur.
The test includes concise Javadoc describing the test scenario (Given/When/Then); there is no excessive or commented-out code and comments add meaningful context rather than stating the obvious.
The test contains no sources of non-determinism (no Random, no time-based calls, no Thread.sleep) and uses only deterministic construction; no external dependencies are present in the method body.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only performs local object creation and does not modify external state, files, or static variables; there is no persistent side-effecting behavior in the method body.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing meaningful categorization for selective execution and indicating appropriate use of labels.
